advisory.finding: With no trust list configured, an unreadable configuration now makes verification return `untrusted` for op-certs that it used to return as `certified`. This contradicts the stated contract that verification is unchanged when the list is unset. `_trust_list_configured` returns True on ANY exception from `compose_config`, so any ConfigError (from any key, or from a malformed rebar.toml/env override) sends every valid op-cert down the trust-list path. `_trust_list_verdict` then fails closed as `untrusted`. scenarios: An environment with no `verify.trusted_opcert_keys` has an invalid value in some unrelated config key, or a malformed env override such as an empty `REBAR_VERIFY_TRUSTED_OPCERT_KEYS`. Every plan-review/completion-verifier op-cert then reads `untrusted`, and the reason blames `verify.trusted_opcert_keys` even though it was never set.
verify_signature library and MCP callers see `verified: false` where they used to see `certified`, even though no trust policy was opted into.
advisory.suggested_fix: Narrow the fail-closed rule to the trust-list key. For other config faults, return False, matching `_required_environment`'s 'unreadable config cannot enable a restriction' contract.
